brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Two full-depth bins provided: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full on two adjacent full bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) joint-bolted; dressed with fork/spoon/knife props to show utensil use.

Configurator verifies only fit and mesh clearance, not materials, sealing or water-tightness. Parts are 3D-printed with layer lines and unsealed joints; no gasket or coating is modeled. Cannot be claimed waterproof regardless of geometry.

Configurator checks only fit/collisions, not material choice, heat resistance, food safety or dishwasher compatibility. 3D-printed plastic safety depends on user-chosen filament and printer; not verified here, so cannot be described as dishwasher safe.

finish.summary: Built a two-cell base with two full-depth bins as a utensil holder and staged utensils. Waterproof and dishwasher-safe claims are unmet: the system cannot verify materials, sealing, heat resistance or food safety - that depends on filament choice and printing. Shape alone does not make it waterproof or dishwasher safe.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
